_about: ECOSYSTEM_V2_PLAN stage 12, the live hour (labels written before any run, 11-20). Work logged from ordinary claude.ai and ChatGPT chats: quiet when nothing is settled, one line for an outcome in the user's own words, one outcome question at most, one entry per thing, and the three-chat relay (Claude Code's lines seeded as rows; ChatGPT reviews; a claude.ai chat is the parent). One invented person per round (setup-work.ts), the work log on; the one-time line set in each site's settings (round A: today's line; round B: the new line, for the A/B); the chats never name Recollect. Graded by grade-work.ts from the simulation database: the work lines each chat's window wrote. 'lines' is the number of new work lines the chat should leave; 'asks' an outcome question in the reply; 'closes' a line on the open line named; 'decides' a decided line on the decision named.

messages: What's the difference between a Postgres advisory lock and SELECT FOR UPDATE, in two lines?
Our CI takes 14 minutes. Any ideas to speed it up?
Caching node_modules sounds good, I'll try it tomorrow.
Out of curiosity, how does Kafka keep ordering within a partition when a producer retries?
For the audit log, should we use a separate table or Postgres logical replication?
Hmm, both have trade-offs. Let me think about it over the weekend.
Draft a short message to my team about moving standup to 10:30.
Not quite, too formal. Leave it, I'll write it myself.
Unrelated, I've started doing a 20 minute walk after lunch every day, it really helps my focus. Anyway, what's a good name for a feature flag that hides the new billing page?
The invoice PDF shows the wrong currency symbol for EUR customers. The template uses locale from the server, not the customer.
Passed the customer's locale into the template like you said. That worked, EUR invoices show € now.
We keep going back and forth on soft deletes for orders. Pros and cons, briefly?
Ok, decided: soft deletes with a deleted_at column, because support needs to restore orders customers delete by mistake.
Quick update on the reporting rewrite: the first three of the five reports now run off the new read model. Can you suggest how to test the remaining two against the old ones?
Help me tighten this incident summary: 'Payments were delayed 40 minutes on Tuesday because a queue consumer crashed on a malformed message.'
Perfect, sent it to the client.
Our cron job sends the weekly digest twice on some Mondays. We run two app instances.
Ok, I'll add a Postgres advisory lock around the job like you showed.
Thanks, that's all for now.
Yes, deployed it and this Monday it sent once.
